rows.note: This is the default noun for fruit preserve, especially when spread on bread or toast.

example.english: I usually spread jam on toast in the morning.
example.traditional: 我朝早通常搽果占喺多士上面。
example.jyutping: ngo5 ziu1 zou2 tung1 soeng4 caa4 gwo2 zem1 hai2 do1 si6 soeng6 min6

rows.note: Use this for congestion or immobilization caused by road traffic.

example.english: There was a traffic jam on the Eastern Corridor during the morning commute, and we couldn't move.
example.traditional: 今日返工時間，東區走廊塞車塞到郁唔到。
example.jyutping: gam1 jat6 faan1 gung1 si4 gaan3 dung1 keoi1 zau2 long4 sak1 ce1 sak1 dou3 juk1 m4 dou2

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice when something blocks a road, passage, or flow.

example.english: There's a jam on the road.

rows.note: Use this when an object or body part becomes stuck in a gap or confined space.

example.jyutping: go3 gwai6 tung2 kaat1 zyu6 zo2

rows.note: Use this when someone forcefully crams something into a tight space.

example.english: I jam the clothes into that tiny box.
example.traditional: 我將啲衫硬塞入個咁細嘅箱入面。
example.jyutping: ngo5 zoeng1 di1 saam1 ngaang6 sak1 jap6 go3 gam3 sai3 ge3 soeng1 jap6 min6

rows.note: Use this for being in trouble or having a difficult situation to deal with.

example.english: We’re really in a jam this time—the document has gone missing.
example.traditional: 我哋今次真係麻煩喇，份文件唔見咗。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 gam1 ci3 zan1 hai6 maa4 faan4 laa3 fan6 man4 gin6 m4 gin3 zo2

rows.note: Use this for playing music spontaneously, especially as an informal group session.

example.traditional: 呢隊樂隊今晚會即興演奏。
example.jyutping: ni1 deoi6 ngok6 deoi6 gam1 maan5 wui5 zik1 hing3 jin2 zau3

rows.note: Use this for a person or thing that is someone’s particular favorite or preference.

example.jyutping: nei1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 hai6 ngo5 sam1 seoi2
